newsitem.title: UK: BA Cargo has no immediate plan for rate rise.
newsitem.headline: BA Cargo has no immediate plan for rate rise.

text.p: British Airways Plc's World Cargo division says it has no immediate plans for an increase in air cargo rates, a spokesman said.
"BA will continue to monitor rates and watch market developments," he told Reuters.
In recent weeks Lufthansa Cargo, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and Air France have all announced plans for cargo rate increases in early 1997, in addition to existing fuel surcharges.
On November 29, Lufthansa Cargo's chairman said there would be an early spring rise of seven percent, which would be followed by further rises next September.
KLM said on December 13 it is planning rate increases of five to 10 percent on certain routes during the first quarter of next year, but did not specify the size of the increases.
Air France's announced on December 20 that it was also a raising in air cargo tariffs and that the increase, which will depend on the routes involved, will be effective by mid-February.
